ground_truth.unit: percentage points of the monthly hiring probability per percentage point of state unemployment
ground_truth.location: Table 1, Panel B, column (1), PE <= 10 x U. Rate
ground_truth.context: Table 1 ("Hiring Over the Business Cycle: With and Without Controls"), Panel B, column (1), row PE <= 10 x U. Rate.  Linear probability model (Equation 1 of the paper) of an indicator equal to 100 if the individual is hired in month t — begins a job at a new firm, either from non-employment in month t-1 or, if employed in t-1, reporting a change of employer since last month; new jobs classified as self-employment are not hires — on an indicator for potential experience (age minus years of education minus six) of at most ten years, and the state monthly unemployment rate interacted with each of the two potential-experience groups (at most ten years; more than ten years), with no main effect of the unemployment rate.  Column (1) has no fixed effects.  Sample: the matched monthly CPS panel, January 1994 to September 2016 (pairs of consecutive months matched on administrative IDs and confirmed on sex, race and age, following Madrian and Lefgren; May-August 1995 and month pairs spanning the eight-month sampling break excluded), civilians over 16 with non-missing age and education, all labour-force statuses in t-1.  Weighted by the average of the two months' CPS sampling weights; standard errors clustered by state (51 including DC).  The coefficient is the young workers' hiring response to one percentage point of state unemployment.

cell.label: claude-code
deviations_manifest: yh_data.csv (about 2 GB) read with data.table::fread(select=) of only the needed columns, to fit the 300 s / 4 GB sandbox (also printed as a DEVIATION line).

The supplied state unemployment file v2unemp_smy.csv covers only Jan 1994 to May 2014. The 2,109,873 person-month pairs from Jun 2014 to Sep 2016 have no unemployment rate and are dropped, so every regression and n_obs_full_sample use Jan 1994 to May 2014 rather than the paper's Jan 1994 to Sep 2016.

Hiring regressions are estimated on cell means (state x month x PE<=10 x demographic cell x t-1 status, with summed weights). Every regressor is constant within a cell, so the WLS point estimates equal the individual-level ones, but the clustered SEs printed are cell-level and are not reported as results.

Years of schooling are imputed from PEEDUCA (31=0, 32=2.5, 33=5.5, 34=7.5, 35=9, 36=10, 37=11, 38=12, 39=12, 40=13, 41/42=14, 43=16, 44=18, 45=20, 46=20). Potential experience = age - schooling - 6; young means PE <= 10.

Sample: age >= 16 (from the t-1 record), valid labour-force status in both months, positive average weight. Demographics, age and education come from the t-1 record. Hire: employed (PEMLR 1-2) in t, with the t job not self-employed (PEIO1COW 6/7), and either not employed in t-1 or employed in t-1 with PUIODP1=2 (different employer). Weight is the average of the two months' PWSSWGT.

Wage regression: hires in t with PRWERNAL=0 (not allocated) and PRERNWA>0, log(PRERNWA/cpi), with averaged CPS weights. Occupation and industry are crosswalked to 2002 codes assuming code years: occupation 1990 (<=2002), 2002 (2003-2010), 2010 (2011+); industry 1990 (<=2002), 2002 (2003-2008), 2007 (2009-2013), 2012 (2014+). Eleven hires with unmatched industry codes are dropped as singleton/NA by fixest.
deviations_stdout: yh_data.csv read with data.table::fread(select=) of the 20 needed columns only (2 GB file, 300 s / 4 GB sandbox)
cell.notes: Independent, blind reproduction from paper.txt only. Attempt-1 was an exploratory variable/timing run that printed no RESULT lines. The final run estimates all 13 quantities with fixest (state, demographic = sex x white x Hispanic x 7 education levels, and month-year FEs, clustered by state) and exits 0 in 295 s, close to the 300 s limit because the column-subset read takes 170-270 s.
